title: Restore an enabled task-record validation CI gate
description:
EDIT: This is rejected and should not be attempted again. The MemorySmith task system should cover task validation and health.

## Summary

Restore a durable, enabled task-record validation gate. The task that introduced the durable task format (CC-093) listed a GitHub Actions workflow validating `Data/Tasks/*.json` as an explicit scope/acceptance item, but after the MemorySmith migration the CI was disabled and is now absent at HEAD. The migration therefore removed its own continuous validation gate at the exact moment schema drift is most likely.

Provenance: `docs/audits/creaturecreator-deep-dive-code-review-audit-26-09-05-23-07-45.md` F1 (P1). Verified at current HEAD `99fe6ad`: no `.github/workflows` exists. Broad owner family: task-system migration / retirement (TSK-0101); CC-093 record is now retired. This is the one clearly net-new accepted item with no clean active owner.

## Scope

- Restore an active GitHub Actions workflow that validates the durable task records in `Data/Tasks/*.json`.
- Keep `Scripts/Test-TaskRecords.ps1` as the authoritative JSON validation step.
- Decide explicitly whether the legacy Markdown tracker validator (`docs/tasks/tools/task_validate.py`) remains required now that the Markdown tracker is frozen; do not silently drop both.
- Name the workflow to describe task-data validation (not generic Unity CI), unless full CI is intentionally in scope.
- Add an acceptance check that the workflow file is present, enabled, and triggered for `push` and `pull_request`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A workflow file exists under `.github/workflows/` that validates `Data/Tasks/*.json` on push and pull_request.
- The validation step runs `Test-TaskRecords.ps1` and fails on malformed records (bad ids/keys/statuses/priorities/duplicates/control characters).
- The legacy-validator decision is explicit and recorded.
- A malformed task record intentionally fails the gate (manual or local proof).

## Validation

Local run of `Scripts/Test-TaskRecords.ps1` over the current tree passes. Confirm the workflow is syntactically valid and its trigger is `push`/`pull_request`. No Unity run is required; this is a repo/tooling gate.

## Findings

- CC-093 acceptance required an automated task-record validation workflow on push/PR.
- Commit `4ac0f72` disabled CI after the MemorySmith migration; no `.github/workflows` directory exists at HEAD, so even a disabled-trigger workflow is gone.
- Two parsers/validators plus a migration layer exist; that is exactly when continuous validation is most valuable.

## Blockers

None known.

## Next Step

Author and enable the workflow; run `Test-TaskRecords.ps1` locally to confirm the current tree passes.

comments.body:
Round 1 BeastMaster sprint — repo/tooling change only. No runtime/editor code or Data/Tasks records touched by hand.

## Implementation
Added `.github/workflows/task-data-validation.yml` (name "Task Data Validation"). It runs on `push` and `pull_request` (both enabled, no path filter for durability) and validates `Data/Tasks/*.json` on every event. The single job checks out the repo and runs `Scripts/Test-TaskRecords.ps1` under `shell: pwsh`; the script throws a terminating error on malformed records (bad ids/keys/statuses/priorities, duplicate ids/keys, invalid JSON, unsafe page slugs, embedded control characters), which fails the step/job/check. Named for task-data validation, not generic Unity CI; no duplicate CI added.

## Legacy-validator decision (explicit, recorded in workflow comments AND here)
`docs/tasks/tools/task_validate.py` (legacy Markdown-tracker validator) is intentionally RETIRED. It is already absent at HEAD, and the Markdown tracker it validated is frozen. `Scripts/Test-TaskRecords.ps1` is the SINGLE source of task-record validation. We do not re-add the Python validator and do not duplicate its checks in YAML. If the Markdown tracker is ever unfrozen, revisit on the task-system family (TSK-0101) before introducing a second validator.

## Validation evidence (exact commands + results)
- `pwsh -NoProfile -File Scripts/Test-TaskRecords.ps1` over current clean `Data/Tasks`: `PASS: Checked 126 task record(s); keys and ids are unique.` exit 0.
- Malformed-record proof (throwaway temp copy, real tree untouched): copied one real record to `%TEMP%`, set `status='BogusStatus'`, ran validator with `-TasksRoot <temp>`: `FAIL ... status 'BogusStatus' is not one of ...` then `throw 'Task record validation failed.'`, exit 1. Gate catches bad data.
- YAML syntactic validity: PyYAML `safe_load` succeeded (`YAML_OK`). Parsed `on` key = `{'push': None, 'pull_request': None}` (both triggers present/enabled; `on` parses as boolean under YAML 1.1 — a known quirk GitHub Actions handles correctly). Job `validate-task-records` present.
- `git diff --check`: exit 0 (no whitespace errors).
- No Unity run required (repo/tooling gate).

## Notes / residual risk / next step
- Working tree shows `Data/Tasks/tsk-0123-restore-task-record-validation-ci-gate.json` modified — that is the MemorySmith task tool persisting this InProgress status update, NOT a manual file edit.
- Not committed/pushed (orchestrator owns that). Remote CI green cannot be proven until push; next step after orchestrator push is to observe the "Task Data Validation" check succeed on a push/PR.
